text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Finance Ministry is putting the final touches to the three state budgets for 1998. They will be tabled to parliament at the end of September.

- A man arrested in connection with the attempted murder of a gambling club owner last month has confessed, and also given police leads in other serious but unsolved crimes committed over the past few years.

- The insistence of (centre right) Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou to run as presidential candidate in next year's elections is causing a headache in the presidential palace. (Kyprianou's party is a junior partner in the government.)
- The status quo in Cyprus is not acceptable or stable, says Britain's special envoy on the Cyprus problem Sir David Hannay.
- Athens has expressed its concern to the United Nations that Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash may attempt to undermine the new mediation effort on Cyprus.

- United Nations experts have drawn up documents on the constitutional aspects of the Cyprus issue, while Britain has a document on the security aspects of the issue in an attempt to bridge the differences between the two sides.
